answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x during the daily settlement peak with heavy writes, so the load-matched move is to add headroom (b3) rather than shed or redirect work. Circuit breaking (b4) fails fast and would drop customer writes, which violates the objective. Replica routing (b5) previously helped write latency only when report reads were contending on the primary; that read-mix is not in evidence here, and settlement writes cannot move to replicas. Rollback (b1) remains a live alternative because a release shipped ~30 minutes before the climb, but the archived case was an error spike, not peak write latency, and undoing a write-path build mid-settlement could interrupt in-flight customer writes. No regional symptom supports failover. Verifying b3 and b1 before treating either summary as decisive. Cause is not isolated, so scale stays a standard increment rather than a broad blast.
